title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity — streaming stability, tool/function calls, roles/stop/logprobs, structured output
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Adds OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity for roles, stop, logprobs, streaming function/tool calls, and structured output. Backwards compatible; see migration notes in docs/openai-compat.md.
description:
Motivation: Customers running OpenAI-compatible clients expect exact behavior from /v1/chat.completions endpoints (roles, name handling, stop tokens, logprobs output, streaming deltas and function/tool calling). This PR implements parity across the API surface and fixes streaming stability issues revealed by long-lived streaming load tests.

This is a behavioral and API-surface change (compat layer) rather than a model change. Key goals: map Redwood internal chat API to OpenAI semantics, preserve existing Redwood endpoints, and keep behavior compatible for existing Redwood users.

Summary of changes: implemented message role/name mapping, stop token handling and partial logprobs output for top-k tokens, deterministic streaming chunk shapes (role presence only in first chunk), stable SSE flushing/backpressure fixes, function/tool calling wire format and function_call: "smart" handling, and structured-output content-type hints. Updated SDKs, added integration tests against openai-compat harness, and expanded docs.

Checklist:
- [x] Role and "name" mapping for messages (user/system/assistant/function).
- [x] stop token semantics (single string, list of strings) and precedence over max_tokens.
- [x] logprobs output for non-streaming and streaming (partial) modes, consistent key names with OpenAI.
- [x] Streaming SSE format: ensure initial message chunk includes role/name when applicable, subsequent deltas only contain content string tokens.
- [x] Stabilize streaming: fixed flush race, added buffer high/low watermarks, and backpressure hooks for runtime.
- [x] Function/tool calling: support function_call policy, dispatch to tools integration layer, and structured output for tool responses.
- [x] Add integration tests and examples in redwood-quickstarts.
- [x] Update openai-compat docs and migration notes.

Notable implementation notes:
- Mapping: messages -> messages with fields {role,name,content} preserved. If a message has a "name" but no role, follow OpenAI rule: default to "user" for name-based senders if appropriate.
- stop handling: We implement stop as a vector of strings; matching is done against raw token stream and generated content post-detokenization to mirror OpenAI behavior. Edge cases (overlapping stops) follow OpenAI precedence documented in docs/openai-compat.md.
- logprobs: Non-streaming logprobs emit full per-token arrays (top_k limited to 5 by default). Streaming emits partial logprobs where first token in a chunk may include a truncated logprobs object; runtime aggregates into final result for non-stream consumers.
- Streaming stability: The main bug was a race between runtime flush and SSE chunk serialization; fixed by serializing on a dedicated streaming worker and adding a per-connection buffer with high/low watermark and an explicit heartbeat every 15s. This prevents stalled connections under high load.
- Function/tool calling: Added an explicit "function_call" field mirrored from OpenAI. When set to {"name":"..."} we route to the named tool; when set to {"auto": true} we evaluate tool-suggest and decide via policy. Tool outputs are returned as assistant messages with role "tool"/"function" per OpenAI semantics.

Testing:
- Unit: parser/mapping tests for messages, stop handling, logprobs shape.
- Integration: end-to-end against openai-compat harness (redwood-eval).
- Load: streaming canary with long-lived streams to validate heartbeat/backpressure.

References: Linear ENG-4823 (chat parity), ENG-4971 (streaming stability), SUP-1024 (customer incident that exposed SSE stall).

Notes for reviewers: The bulk of the changes are in openai_compat mapping, api handler glue, and runtime streaming worker. SDK changes are small and backward compatible. See changed_files for details.
commits: fix(streaming): serialize SSE in dedicated worker, add buffer watermarks and heartbeat
feat(functions): add function_call routing and tool response shaping
test: add openai-compat integration tests and quickstart example
docs: update openai-compat.md and migration notes
review_comments: Daniel Kim: Please confirm the role/name precedence when both are present; observed a mismatch with the original OpenAI doc in one unit test.
Sofia Patel (author): Updated mapping to prefer explicit role if present, otherwise infer from name for backwards compatibility with older clients. Added unit tests to cover both cases.
Riley Thompson: Streaming worker looks safer, but can we reduce default heartbeat to 10s for mobile clients?
Sofia Patel (author): Kept 15s default to reduce noise on long-lived desktop sessions; added config flag STREAM_HEARTBEAT_SECS to allow tuning per deployment (docs updated).
Priya Shah: The logprobs shape for streaming is tricky; ensure downstream SDK aggregates correctly. Add a comment to SDK implementations.
Sofia Patel (author): Added SDK aggregation notes and a helper in sdk/python/openai_compat.py to reconstruct final logprobs.
merge_commit_message:
openai: /v1/chat.completions parity — roles, stop, logprobs, streaming, function calls, structured output

Squashed commits: feat(openai_compat) + fix(streaming) + feat(functions) + test + docs
notes_for_ops: Deploy note: new STREAM_HEARTBEAT_SECS config with default 15s. Rolling deploy recommended to avoid temporary double-processing of streaming workers during rollout. Monitor streaming_connections_active metric and streaming_buffered_bytes for spikes after rollout.
migration_notes: Existing Redwood clients that rely on the older streaming shape should continue to work; we added a feature flag OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT_MODE for stricter OpenAI matching. See docs/openai-compat.md for details.
